question.text: Mole fraction of the toluene in the vapour phase which is in equilibrium with a solution of benzene <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> and toluene <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">p</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> having 2.0 moles of each, is

solution.text:
Mole fraction of toluene vapour =pToXTPToXT+pBoXB

XT= Mole fraction of toluene in solution =2/4 = 0.5

XB= Mole fraction of benzene = 2/4 = 0.5

pTo= Vapour pressure of pure toluene = 80 mm

pTo= Vapour pressure of benzene = 120 mm

=80×45.80+120×0.5=0.40
